newsitem.title: USA: Clinton "very pleased" with budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Clinton "very pleased" with budget deal.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was "very pleased" with a tentative balanced budget and tax-cutting deal reached with Congressional leaders on Monday, White House aides said.

"The President was pleased with the information and was looking forward to a full briefing in the morning," White House spokesman Lockhart told reporters in Las Vegas, where Clinton was wrapping up a three-day trip to the Western United States.

Lockhart said that White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles had called an aide who was with the president and told him that a tentative deal had been reached. At 4:30 p.m. PDT (7:30 EDT) the aide reached Clinton on the golf course at the Las Vegas Country Club, where the president was golfing with basketball superstar Michael Jordan and some state governors.
Clinton sought and received assurances that three issues had been taken care of: more spending for education, a child tax credit, and an expansion of health benefits for poor children, Lockhart said.
"It is possible that he'll make some sort of statement tomorrow to talk about the significance of what's gone on today," Lockhart said.
